Mia: Heads-up: saw a weird MRR jump on the long-tail cohort after yesterday's 4-bit reranker rollout. NDCG unchanged, but MRR +12% for tail only. Figured it's a bug — anyone else seeing this?
Sam: Yep, saw it in the smoke run. Full eval: top1 up, ranks 2-5 down. Smells like a tiebreaker / softmax calibration issue after quantization. Any candidate-ordering differences?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled back quantized-reranker:v2 at 2026-03-18T22:10Z due to parity alerts on rerank metrics.
Dain: Which split exactly? tail cohort name? seed fixed? Was there a change to priming or query concat?
Mia: Tail = user_queries_longtail_2026-02 (holdout). Seed=42. Priming / prompt templates were unchanged. We ran with batch_size=32 and KV cache ON.
Rachel: Check tokenizer normalization and whitespace trimming. Long-tail queries often have stray punctuation that can flip logits. Also confirm embed/logit scaling — int4 can clip/shift logits if scale tables are wrong.
Sam: I'll run a small repro now. Command: ```python eval.py --model rerank-int4 --split tail_cohort_v4 --seed 42 --batch 32 --log topk``` Should finish in ~10m and push artifacts to /tmp/rerank_int4_repro.
Tony: Please dump raw logits for the top 10 examples. I want to inspect topk margins. If top1>top2 margin ballooned post-quant, that's a calibration shift, not quality.
Mia: Pasting a couple quick samples we captured: sample_id=98765 pre-quant logits=[2.1, 1.9, 1.2], post-int4 logits=[3.4, 0.2, 0.1] — that's massive. Looks like a scale mismatch on the final linear.
Dain: OK that's the smoking gun. Likely missing per-channel scale for the final dense or a wrong dequant step in the compile. Check compilation flags for per-channel vs per-tensor quant.
Sam: Opening a PR to force per-channel scales on the final projection + added a small unit test that compares topk margins vs float baseline. Will canary to 10% traffic.
Rachel: :thumbsup: Also add a QA gate that computes KL/divergence on topk margin distributions between float and quant on the bringup harness. If KL>threshold, fail deploy.
Mia: Thanks — assigning follow-ups (Sam: repro + PR, Dain: compile flags + kernel check, Tony: histogram tests). I'll post the canary results here when available.
